RAG Chatbot — High-Level Overview
Multi-tenant AI chatbot platform with organization-based document sharing, voice I/O, embeddable widget, and quota management
Who Uses It

👨‍💻 Developer (Superadmin)
• Full system access
• Create clients, manage settings
• Configure AI providers
• Manage embed widgets
• View all data across all orgs

🏢 Admin (Org Manager)
• Manage users in their org
• Create departments
• Upload documents
• View org-scoped data

💬 User
• Chat with AI (text + voice)
• Upload files (if permitted)
• Download shared forms
• View own usage & preferences

🤖 API Client / Robot
• External system via API key
🌐 Embed Widget User
• Chat via embedded widget on 3rd-party site
What It Does

📄 Document Upload & Vectorization
Upload PDF, DOCX, Excel, images, text files
Auto-OCR → chunk → embed → store in vector DB
Shared to selected organizations

💬 AI Chat (RAG)
Ask questions → search relevant docs
→ AI generates answer with sources
Org-scoped: only sees shared documents
Chat history saved per session

🎤 Voice Input & Output
Speak → transcribe → chat → TTS response
Continuous mode: hands-free conversation
Auto-detects silence, interrupts TTS on speech

🌐 Embeddable Widget
Paste one script tag on any website
Fully themed chat popup (colors, logo, shape)
Users login and chat with same AI

📊 Quota & Plan Management
Storage limits per plan
Chat quotas (individual or shared pool)
Monthly auto-renewal

📋 Forms & Downloads
Upload downloadable forms
AI can suggest form downloads in chat
Download tracking with stats

🔑 API Access
External systems chat via API key
Native mode (uses internal RAG) or Webhook mode (forwards to n8n)
Robot integration endpoints

In one sentence:
A self-hostable, multi-tenant AI chatbot platform where organizations upload documents, and users chat with an AI that answers from those documents — with voice support, embeddable widgets, quota management, and role-based access control.

RAG Chatbot Architecture
Current implementation based on server.js, chatPipeline.js, uploadPipeline.js, frontend/, public/embed/, glmocr-service/

Reality note
Backend is a monolithic Express app in server.js.
Duplicate/legacy route blocks exist. Daily cleanup job runs automatically.
See pages 6-9 for Voice, Embed Widget, Quota/Billing, Robot/API details.

Upload and Chat RAG Pipelines
A. Upload / Vectorization Flow

1. User uploads file
/api/upload
multipart form-data
sharedWith[] + type=document/form

2. server.js
Check storage quota
Save file to local uploads or S3
Insert Mongo files metadata
Write audit log

3. Only for documents:
Open SSE stream to frontend
Call processUploadedFile(...)

4. Detect file category
OCR, docx, excel, plain text

5. Text extraction path
PDF: pdf-parse first
Image/PDF OCR if needed
DOCX: mammoth
Excel: xlsx to CSV
Text: fs read

6. OCR providers
Offline: GLM OCR service
Online: Mistral OCR or Google Document AI

7. Chunk pages
chunkText(text, chunkSize, overlap)
Payload includes file_id, file_name, page_number, chunk_index, shared_with, uploader metadata

8. Embed chunks
Offline default: Ollama
Online options: OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral

9. Store vectors
Default/offline: Qdrant collection documents
Optional online: Pinecone

10. Update Mongo file doc
Set vectorized=true, chunks, pages
If S3 upload succeeded, remove local temp file

11. Frontend receives SSE progress
upload → ocr → preview → chunking → embedding → storing → done
B. Chat / Retrieval Flow

1. Entry points
/api/chat browser
/api/embed/chat embed
/api/v1/chat API key native mode

2. Save user message into Mongo messages
sessionId, chatType, chatName, org context, startedBy

3. Quota checks (browser chat)
Resolve user group from organization
Read groups, chat_counts, chat_resets

4. processBrowserChat()
Resolve accessible organizations from user_organization_assignments + org hierarchy

5. Embed user query
Provider from chat settings:
Ollama / OpenAI / Gemini

6. Search vectors
Qdrant or Pinecone
Filter by org shared_with
Optional fileId filter
Limit = chatMaxChunks

7. Build final prompt
System prompt + document context block
+ last 20 messages from Mongo history
+ current user question

8. Call chat LLM
Gemini / OpenAI / Groq / Ollama Cloud / Ollama Local

9. Deduplicate sources
file_name + page_number

10. Save bot message
response text + sources + responseTimeMs
respect user preferences: showSources / verboseMode

11. Increment chat count
Only when user belongs to quota group

12. Return response to UI/client
Browser and embed return text + sources + sessionId
API key endpoint returns text/speak split

Webhook alternative
/api/v1/chat can bypass native RAG
Forward request to API-key-specific n8n webhook

Delete path
DELETE /api/files/:id
remove Mongo file doc
delete from S3/local
deleteFileVectors()

Boss-level summary
This repo is a self-hostable multi-tenant RAG chat platform with org-scoped document sharing, offline/online AI processing options, optional embed widget, API key access, quotas, and admin operations.

Organization Hierarchy and File Access
Based on organizations, user_organization_assignments, files.sharedWith, chatPipeline.js, and file endpoints in server.js
A. Organization Data Model

organizations collection
Each node stores:
name, type, parentId, path, groupId

Organization
type = organization
Top-level client/company node

Entity
type = entity
Child under organization

Department
type = department
Can sit under entity or organization

Hierarchy fields
parentId links node to parent
path stores name chain array, e.g. ["Org A", "Entity X", "Dept HR"]

user_organization_assignments
Maps user to one or more org nodes
userId + organizationId
This is the real access anchor for users/admins

Who can create what
Developer: organization + entity + department
Admin: only department, and only under assigned org hierarchy
assigned to node(s)
B. File Sharing and Visibility

files collection
Important fields:
type, userId, groupId, sharedWith[], isDownloadable, isVectorized, url

Upload sharing model
Uploader picks one or more organizations/departments
Backend stores selected org IDs into files.sharedWith
Same list is also passed into vector payload as shared_with

File list / download access (as implemented)
Non-developer user gets their assigned orgs
+ backend adds parent orgs from path
User can see/download file if sharedWith intersects that set

Chat retrieval access (as implemented)
getUserAccessibleOrgIds() takes direct assignments
+ tries to include child orgs via hierarchy lookup
Vector search filters on payload shared_with

Forms access
Forms are stored in same files collection with type=form
Form endpoints use slightly different visibility logic from document listing

Developer visibility
Developer bypasses most restrictions and can view all files, widgets, users, logs, etc.
used by /api/files + download
used by chat vector payload
C. Example Hierarchy

Organization
ABC Holdings

Entity
ABC Manufacturing

Entity
ABC Services

Example user assignment
User assigned to ABC Manufacturing / HR

File A sharedWith = [ABC Holdings]
Visible to users whose file access includes parent org

File B sharedWith = [HR]
Visible only if user has HR node in their effective access set
D. Important Implementation Note

Access logic is not perfectly uniform across the app
Chat retrieval path and file listing/download path do not derive hierarchy exactly the same way.

Chat pipeline
Uses direct org assignments + tries to include child orgs when searching vectors.
Source: chatPipeline.js / getUserAccessibleOrgIds()

File list/download
Uses direct org assignments + parent org names from path when checking visible sharedWith values.
Source: /api/files and /api/files/:id/download

Presentation-safe wording
You can explain to boss that the system supports hierarchical organization-based sharing, but implementation today still has some legacy inconsistencies between modules because backend is concentrated in one big file.

Role Matrix and Visibility Rules
Complete boss-facing explanation of who can create, manage, and see which data in the current implementation
A. Main Roles in Current System

Developer
Top-level superuser in practice
Can see all users, all files, all organizations, all API keys, settings, audit, deleted chats, embed widgets

Admin
Scoped manager under assigned organization hierarchy
Can manage users/orgs in limited ways
Sees assigned org and related child scope depending on endpoint

User
Normal authenticated user
Can chat, view own accessible files/forms, use own organization scope, update own account/preferences

API Key Client
External system using x-api-key
Operates as mapped user context
Can use native mode or webhook mode

Embed User
Logs in through widget
Actually authenticates against same users collection
Then chats through embed endpoints

Practical note
There are also legacy RBAC collections (roles, permissions), but much of real behavior is still controlled directly by req.user.role checks.
B. Who Can Create / Manage What
Legend: Green = yes, Yellow = limited, Red = no
Create organization / entity
Create department
Yes, but only under assigned org hierarchy
Create / edit users
Yes, limited to admin scope and non-developer users
Upload document / form
Yes, if user canUploadFiles not disabled
Yes, if canUploadFiles true
Manage provider keys / app settings / embed widgets / API keys
Mostly no
See audit logs / deleted chats / download tracking
Audit logs only; not deleted chats/download tracking pages
C. What Each Role Can See

Developer sees
- all files and forms
- all organizations and users
- all sessions and API usage
- all embed widgets and settings
- all quotas/groups
- can delete any chat session

Admin sees
- users in assigned org scope
- organizations in assigned tree
- files/forms shared into accessible scope
- audit logs for own org scope
- cannot see developer account
- cannot manage global technical settings

User sees
- own chats and sessions
- own account, preferences, storage/quota view
- documents/forms allowed by org-sharing logic
- no admin pages

File visibility rule
File visibility depends mainly on files.sharedWith intersecting the user effective org set, except developer who sees all.

Chat visibility rule
Chat retrieval depends on vector payload shared_with and effective org IDs from assignment logic in chatPipeline.js.

Delete file rule
Uploader or developer can delete a file.
Delete operation also removes vector entries from Qdrant/Pinecone.

Download rule
Forms must be marked downloadable.
Non-developer must pass org-based access check before direct/local or S3 download URL is returned.

Caution for boss discussion
Best accurate phrase: 'access is organization-based and hierarchical, but current implementation has some endpoint-level variation because the backend evolved inside one large service file'.
D. Practical Visibility Scenarios

Scenario 1
User assigned to Department HR
File shared to HR
Result: visible

Scenario 2
User assigned to Department HR
File shared to parent Organization
Result: usually visible in file list/download path

Scenario 3
User assigned to Department HR
File shared only to sibling Department Finance
Result: not visible

Scenario 4
Developer opens Files page
Any file regardless of sharedWith
Result: visible

Scenario 5
Admin assigned to organization root
Child department file shared in same tree
Result: usually visible

Scenario 6
API client uses key tied to user context
Native mode chat with org-limited vectors
Result: access follows mapped user/org scope

Scenario 7
Embed widget user logs in using same platform account
Embed chat still uses same RAG scope logic
Result: not public, still user-scoped

Scenario 8
Form uploaded with downloadable=true
Endpoint logic for forms differs slightly from docs
Result: verify by endpoint, not by assumption

Best final explanation to boss
1. Files are shared to org nodes.
2. Users inherit visibility from assigned hierarchy logic.
3. Developer sees everything.
4. Admin sees managed scope.
5. Some older endpoints still need harmonization.

Voice Input, TTS Output, and Continuous Conversation Mode
Based on ChatInput.tsx, ChatMessage.tsx, server.js /api/transcribe and /api/tts endpoints
A. Speech-to-Text (STT) Flow

1. User clicks mic button
or continuous mode active
ChatInput.tsx starts recording

2. Browser mode:
Web Speech API
SpeechRecognition
No server call needed

3. API mode:
MediaRecorder captures audio
POST /api/transcribe
multipart audio blob

4. Server STT providers:
• Gemini (generateContent with audio)
• Mistral Voxtral
• ElevenLabs
• External webhook
• Local Whisper (Ollama)

5. Returns transcribed text
Inserted into chat input box
Language: auto/en/ms/zh/ta/multi

Language mapping
Frontend maps language codes to provider-specific formats.
Settings configurable in SettingsPage Voice tab.
B. Text-to-Speech (TTS) Flow

1. User clicks Play on bot message
or auto-TTS in continuous mode
ChatMessage.tsx strips markdown

2. POST /api/tts
Body: { text, language }

3. Server TTS providers:
• Gemini (parallel chunk → PCM → WAV merge)
• Google Cloud Long Audio (auto lang: EN/ZH/MS/TA)
• Mistral Voxtral
• ElevenLabs

4. Returns audio buffer
Frontend plays via AudioContext
Dispatches ttsStarted/ttsEnded events

Gemini TTS detail
Long text split into chunks, each sent in parallel to Gemini.
Raw PCM responses merged and converted to WAV with proper headers.
C. Continuous Conversation Mode (Radio Button)

1. User clicks Radio button
Continuous mode activates
Auto-starts listening

2. Silence detection
Browser mode: 2s silence timeout
Gemini mode: AudioContext analyser
monitors volume, 2s silence threshold

3. On silence detected:
Stop recording
Transcribe (browser or API)
Auto-send message to chat

4. Bot responds
Auto-TTS plays response
Listening paused during TTS
ttsStarted/ttsEnded events

5. TTS ends → auto-resume listening
Cycle repeats until user
clicks Radio button again to stop

Interrupt detection
If user speaks during TTS playback:
• TTS audio stops immediately
• Listening resumes
• New speech captured

State sync via localStorage
continuousMode — active flag
continuousModeMessage — pending text
ttsPlaying — TTS active flag
ttsBlocking — block listening during TTS

UI Status indicators
• Listening... (green pulse)
• Speaking... (user talking)
• Transcribing... (API processing)
• Bot speaking... (TTS playing)

Full cycle:
Listen → Silence → Transcribe → Send → Bot Reply → Auto-TTS → TTS End → Listen again

Interrupt: User speaks during TTS → Stop TTS → Listen → new cycle

Embed Widget System
Embeddable chat widget for third-party websites. Managed via EmbedWidgetsPage.tsx, served from public/embed/
A. Deployment Flow

1. Developer creates widget
in EmbedWidgetsPage
Sets theme, colors, shape,
domains, system prompt

2. Widget saved to
embed_widgets collection
Gets unique widgetId

3. Embed code generated:
<script src=".../widget.js"
data-widget-id="...">
Client pastes into their site

4. widget.js creates iframe
pointing to chat.html?widgetId=...
Listens for postMessage resize

5. chat.html loads config
GET /api/embed/config/:widgetId
Applies theme, colors, logo
B. Theming Options

Appearance
Theme: light / dark / auto
Main color + gradient
Button shape: circle / rounded / square
Bubble style: modern / rounded / sharp / pill
Font size: sm / md / lg
Window roundness slider
Header logo + button icon upload
Powered-by toggle

Content
Header title + subtitle
Welcome message
Input placeholder text

Settings
Allowed domains (comma-separated)
Custom system prompt
Active / inactive toggle
C. Embed Chat Flow

Login
POST /api/embed/login
Same users collection
JWT stored per widgetId in localStorage

Chat
POST /api/embed/chat
Uses same RAG pipeline
Org-scoped vector search
Widget system prompt override

Features
Session persistence per widget
Basic markdown rendering
Typing indicator
User avatar menu + logout
iframe resize via postMessage

D. Embed API Endpoints
GET /api/embed/config/:widgetId — public, no auth
POST /api/embed/login — public, returns JWT
POST /api/embed/chat — auth required
GET /api/embed/messages — auth required
GET /api/embed/sessions — auth required
Admin CRUD: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/embed-widgets
POST /api/embed-widgets/upload-logo

Quota System, Plans, and Client Onboarding
Based on groups collection, chat_counts, chat_resets, GroupsPage.tsx, NewClientPage.tsx, /api/create-client
A. Plans / Groups System

groups collection
name — plan name
storageLimitGB — max storage
chatQuota — 0 = unlimited
quotaType — individual or total
renewDay — day of month (1-31)
bonusQuota — extra allowance

Quota types
Individual: each user in group gets own quota
Total: entire group shares one pool

Tracking collections
chat_counts — groupId + userId + month + count
chat_resets — groupId + month + resetAt
Auto-resets on renewDay each month

Admin actions (GroupsPage)
Create/edit/delete plans
Assign orgs to plans
Reset quota manually
Add bonus quota
Change renew day

Storage enforcement
Upload checks group storageLimitGB
Sums file sizes for group
Rejects if over limit
B. Client Onboarding (NewClientPage)

1. Developer fills form:
Organization name
Admin full name + email + password
Plan selection

2. POST /api/create-client
Creates all in one transaction:
• Organization node
• Admin user (role=admin, mustChangePassword)
• user_organization_assignment
• Links org to selected plan

3. Admin logs in first time
Forced password change
Then can manage their org
C. Provider Keys (Global + Per-Org Override)

provider_keys collection
Global: _id: 'keys'
Per-org: _id: 'keys_{orgId}'
Fields: geminiKey, openaiKey, mistralKey, groqKey, googleCloudKey

Resolution logic
resolveProviderKeys(orgId)
1. Load global keys
2. Load org-specific keys
3. Org keys override global (non-empty fields only)
4. Also syncs to settings collection

ProviderKeysPage UI
Org selector: Global + per-client
Providers: Gemini, OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, Google Cloud
Each: key input + show/hide + status indicator
Google Cloud accepts service account JSON
D. Operational: Daily Cleanup + Testing

cleanupOldData()
Runs daily on server start
Deletes old deleted_messages, audit_logs,
download_tracking, api_usage
Based on settings retention days

Test endpoints
POST /api/test-webhook — verify webhook URL
POST /api/test-s3 — verify S3 credentials

Re-embed (developer only)
POST /api/reembed — SSE progress
Re-processes all files when embedding
model/dimension changes
